recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as the final reconciliation for FHIR-13050. No follow-up source work is needed unless a future work-group decision changes the global HEAD policy.
issue_request: FHIR-13050 asked to add HEAD support everywhere GET is allowed, add HEAD to Bundle.entry.request.method, and state that servers without HEAD support must respond according to HTTP, such as 405 Method Not Allowed or 501 Not Implemented.
initial_application: The change was applied by explicit December 2017 #13050 commits: 4b3c2b6858b70b4b2342c48ac651412b5ebf7e8e added the RESTful HEAD narrative to source/http.html, and 2fdaaabe2bfee3f85e5dc9b320fab3d9a69b0442 added HEAD to the Bundle request-method spreadsheet source. Later source rework preserved that content in the current Bundle StructureDefinition and HTTPVerb CodeSystem.
additional_context: Bundle is active in source/fhir.ini, and the current source files under source/bundle are build-scope inputs. FHIR-40497 later clarified nearby vread wording around HEAD for R6 but did not reverse or narrow the global HEAD rule. Community searches found only a tracker bot notification in Zulip and no direct Confluence references that alter the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. source/bundle/structuredefinition-Bundle.xml lists Bundle.entry.request.method as GET | HEAD | POST | PUT | DELETE | PATCH, source/bundle/codesystem-http-verb.xml defines the HEAD code in the required HTTPVerb code system, and source/http.html says HEAD is allowed anywhere GET is used and unsupported HEAD follows HTTP error behavior.

related_jiras.note: A later Applied R6 clarification of vread wording around HEAD; it supports that HEAD behavior remains current but is a separate editorial issue, not part of this seed decision.
